articleTitle: Transmission Improvement in Fiber Radio Links using Semiconductor Laser
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This investigation experimentally demonstrates the performance improvement in fiber- radio links by using a semiconductor laser. This technique improves receiver sensitivity over 4.5 dB by increasing the optical modulation depth.

articleTitle: Band Edge effects in Photonic Crystal Waveguides: Polarisation Conversion
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Narrowband polarisation conversion from TE to TM and back is observed at the quasi- TE transmission band edge of a linear photonic SOI photonic crystal waveguide.

articleTitle: Hybrid Packet/Circuit SCM Optical Label Switching Node With Priority Based Routing Capabilities
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a 10 Gb/s hybrid optical node with a built-in controller programmed to identify circuit and packet connections and make the routing decisions including contention resolution schemes according to the label priority information.

articleTitle: Multi-bound Solitons in a FM Mode-locked Fiber Laser
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report, for the first time, experimental observation of multi-solitons in an active FM mode-locked fiber laser. Not only bound soliton pairs but also triple- and quadruple-soliton bound states can be generated.

articleTitle: All-Order PMD Compensation via VIPA Based Pulse Shaper
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrated full compensation of ~ 15 ps optical pulses distorted by all-order polarization mode dispersion (PMD) effects to more than 100 ps by using a virtually imaged phased-array (VIPA) based transmission pulse shaper.

articleTitle: Versatile-PON Service for Next Generation Optical Access Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel optical access networks with a function of versatile adaptable architecture is proposed and demonstrated. The versatile-PON service is successfully demonstrated by both E-PON and WDM-PON with a simple uni-architecture of remote node.

articleTitle: A Lensed Fiber for Butt Coupling Between High-Index Contrast Waveguides and Single-Mode Fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A lensed fiber with a convex-piano silicon microlens is proposed for butt-coupling between standard single-mode fibers and high-index contrast waveguides with fine mode-field diameters. The theoretical focused spot diameter is 0.56 μm at the wavelength 1.55 μm.

articleTitle: New Results on the Efficiency of Bismuth Fiber Lasers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: CW Bi fiber laser slope efficiency of 32% at 1160 nm is obtained at room temperature; at 77K it reaches 52%. The model is proposed explaining the dependence of efficiency on temperature and pump power.

articleTitle: Reprogrammable Optical Phased Array Switching
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel reprogrammable optical phase array (ROPA) device is presented as a reconfigurable electro-optic element. One specific application of the ROPA, a 1:6 electro-optic space switch, is fully described.

articleTitle: Preamble Delaying Label Update Mechanism for Self-routed Optical Packet Switching Nerks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper proposes a novel label update mechanism by delaying preamble for self-routed optical packet switching networks. The experimental results on our node implementation show the feasibility of the proposed mechanism.

articleTitle: Wavelength-Retaining 1 × 2 Optical Router for DPSK Signal Using Nonlinear Polarization Rotation in a SOA
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a wavelength-retaining optical switch for DPSK signal using nonlinear polarization rotation in a SOA. The bit-rate transparent 1x2 optical router operates over 20 nm with a power penalty less than 3 dB.

articleTitle: Compact All-Fiber Interrogation Unit for FBG sensors
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A two-mode photonic crystal fiber interferometer (PCF) is proposed as a low-cost interrogation unit for FBG-based sensors. The interferometer consists of a piece of index-guiding PCF fusion spliced between two standard single-mode fibers. At the splices the voids of the PCF are sealed allowing the excitation of only two modes. The interferometer exhibits ripples from 800 to 1600 nm with high fringe contrast and behaves as a variable filter in that range. The Bragg wavelength shift is converted into intensity changes which can be measured accurately and in realtime. Detection of wavelength shifts of 2 pm is feasible with the proposed unit which is comparable to state-of-the-art FBG interrofgators.

articleTitle: Fiber Lasers for Secure Key Distribution
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We study a new concept for secure key distribution based on establishing laser oscillations between sender and receiver. The eavesdropping difficulty can be increased arbitrarily, making it an intriguing alternative to quantum key distribution systems.

articleTitle: All-Optical Sampling in a Multiple Quantum Well Saturable Absorber
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The use of multiple-quantum-well saturable absorbers in all optical sampling of high repetition rate pulse trains is presented. Measurements of a 40 GHz pulse train were made using a device with a response time of 5 ps.

articleTitle: Prevention of Quality Degradation in Optical Fiber Interconnects for Last 1 Mile
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Study focuses on prevention of quality degradation in optical interconnects in the last mile. This report looks at ways for quality improvements during connection, how to understand and apply procedures for the fiber construction field.

articleTitle: All-fiber 1085-nm wide supercontinuum source based on a mode-locked ytterbium fiber laser with dispersion compensation by a chirped fiber Bragg grating
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The pulses of an ytterbium-fiber laser with dispersion compensation provided by a chirped fiber Bragg grating are amplified in a core-pumped fiber amplifier and broadened in a photonic crystal fiber to an octave spanning supercontinuum.

articleTitle: Rapidly Tunable Optical Add Drop Multiplexer in Ti:LiNbO3 Utilizing Non-polarizing Beam Splitters
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A polarization-independent four-port electro-optic tunable filter in the 1530 nm wavelength regime utilizing non-polarizing relaxed beam splitters and strain-induced polarization converters on LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> with 16nm tuning range and 46 ns tuning speed is reported.

articleTitle: Ultra-small Photonic Crystal Lasers Near Communication Wavelengths
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Recent progresses on wavelength-scale photonic crystal lasers are reported. Electrically-driven nondegenerate photonic crystal lasers and reconfigurable microfiber-coupled photonic crystal waveguide lasers are discussed in detail. Schemes enabling optical coupling in excess of 80% are also proposed.

articleTitle: Linear and resonant nonlinear optical properties of Ag-nanocrystals incorporated germano-silicate fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Germano-silicate glass fiber containing silver nanocrystals was developed by modified chemical vapor deposition and solution doping processes. The SPR absorption band appeared centering at 501nm and the resonant nonlinear refractive index at 1549nm was 5.4><;10@quot;16m2/W.

articleTitle: Reduction of Multimode Interference in 300-nm Broadband Cr-Doped Fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Reduction of multimode interference in 300-nm broadband Cr-doped fibers (CDFs) using mode-field matched center launching technique is demonstrated. With a matched CDF core diameter around 15.5 μm, the measured broadband coupling efficiencies are 60.3%~ 87.5%. This study may open the possibility for utilizing the CDFs as a new broadband fiber amplifier to cover 300 nm bandwidths.

articleTitle: Automated Performance Equalization in WDM Networks with inline Optical Add Drop Multiplexers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a novel pre-emphasis technique that, knowing pre-FEC BER values, automatically optimizes the performance margins of WDM channels in a line with OADM's. We successfully tested it using commercial equipment.

articleTitle: Stabilized Optical Frequency Combs from Diode Lasers - Applications in Optical Communications, Signal Processing and Instrumentation
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The development of compact sources of stabilized optical frequency combs from semiconductor diode lasers will be reviewed. Applications in coherent communications and signal processing will be suggested and highlighted.

articleTitle: Statistics of Crosstalk in Fiber Optical Parametric Amplification
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Amplification of wavelength-division multiplexed data in parametric devices introduces channel cross-talk. We develop a model to obtain correct statistics and predict different properties such as how bit-errors are introduced and their dependence on fiber properties.

articleTitle: Traffic Aggregation for Peer-to-Peer File Delivery in Optical Backbone Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose traffic aggregation for peer-to-peer file delivery in optical backbone networks with the objective of minimizing the total traffic and blocking rate. Two algorithms are discussed and evaluated via simulation.

articleTitle: Pseudowire Packet Loss Control in Optical Access
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We introduce a packet loss control mechanism to emulate the delivery of native services over packet switched network (PSN) using pseudowire (PW). We propose the virtual circuit connectivity verification (VCCV) insertion (VI) algorithm for adapting variable bit rate (VBR) PW rates to the dynamics of PSN tunnel. Our approach is compatible to existing PW standards, and its applicability has been demonstrated by analysis.

articleTitle: High Frequency Spectral Domain QKD Architecture with Dispersion Management for WDM Network
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report a new quantum key distribution scheme based on phase coding in frequency domain including active compensation dispersion and polarisation insensitive receiver. An experimental system demonstrated stable quantum bit error up to 15 hours.

articleTitle: Comparison of 100Gb/s transmission performances between RZ-DQPSK and polarization multiplexed NRZ/RZ-DPSK with automatic polarization de-multiplexer
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Long-term transmission performances of polarization multiplexed 2x50 Gb/s NRZ/RZ-DPSK signals, denoting good transmission performances but with larger PMD-induced BER fluctuations compared with 100 Gb/s RZ-DQPSK, are successfully observed by constructing an automatic polarization de-multiplexer.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Induced Form-Birefringence and PMD in Dispersion-Compensating Hole-Assisted Fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The birefringence and polarization-mode dispersion characteristics of dispersion-compensating hole-assisted fibers are analyzed numerically. It is revealed that distortion in air-holes leads to high birefringence and also shifts the dispersion by ±2% to its optimum value.

articleTitle: Dispersion Trimming Using a Liquid Crystal on Silicon Based Wavelength Selective Switch
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The functionality of an LCOS-based wavelength selective switch is extended to do dispersion trimming, tunable per channel and output port. We experimentally demonstrate pulse splitting with different dispersion settings in each of the split signals.

articleTitle: Magneto-optical isolator with SOI waveguide
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A magneto-optical isolator with SOI waveguides is demonstrated. The isolator is fabricated by direct-bonding a magneto-optic garnet onto the SOI waveguides. Nonreciprocal phase shift is observed and the isolation ratio of 21 dB is obtained.

articleTitle: Compact Multiwavelength Laser Source Based on Cascaded InP-Microdisks Coupled to One SOI Waveguide
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A compact multiwavelength laser source, which consists of four cascaded InP-microdisks coupled to one SOI waveguide, is introduced for WDM purposes. Equally distributed laser peaks and low crosstalk were obtained with the proposed structure.

articleTitle: All-Optical Contention Resolution with TTL-Aware Selective 3R Regeneration in Optical-Label Switching Router Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper experimentally demonstrates error-free all-optical contention resolution of asynchronous, variable-length, and mix-data rate packets in Optical-Label-Switching router networks. Time-To-Live information triggers selective 3R regeneration in the router.

articleTitle: A Novel Optical Phase Locking technique based on Single Side Sub-Carrier modulation
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel optical phase locking technique based on single side sub-carrier-modulation is presented and experimentally demonstrated. This technique reduces the LO spurious spectral components in order to avoid interference in the UDWDM coherent demodulation operations.

articleTitle: Terahertz Transmitters and Receivers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: THz spectroscopy promises attractive applications in various fields. Commercial use requires compact, room temperature and cost effective systems. The role of telecom technology and recent developments on novel InP devices are summarized in this paper.

articleTitle: 40 GHz Bright and Dark Parabolic Pulse Generation Using a Picosecond Optical Pulse Source and a 64-channel AWG
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: 40 GHz parabolic pulse generation by the spectral manipulation of a picosecond optical pulse is demonstrated. Bright and dark parabolic pulses were generated from a mode-locked fiber laser using a 64-channel AWG pulse shaper.

articleTitle: Novel Chirp-Enhanced Tunable Fast Light of Ultra-Short Pulses in Semiconductor Optical Amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Large tunable advance and delay are demonstrated by varying the sign and magnitude of the linear chirp of 440 fs pulses using ultrafast nonlinearities in semiconductor optical amplifiers, for the first time.

articleTitle: 10 Gb/s Long-Reach Optical Access with Multi-Mode Fiber Distribution Using Baseband Single-Sideband OFDM
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report a 10 Gb/s repeater-based optical access system using baseband single- sideband OFDM. The system enables transmission through 100 km feeder fiber and 500 m distribution multi-mode fibers and use of directly modulated VCSELs at customer premises.

articleTitle: Fast Measurement of Polarization Mode Dispersion via Virtually Imaged Phased-Array Based Spectral Polarimetry
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate fast measurement of polarization mode dispersion (PMD) with large range (differential group delay <;90ps) via high speed spectral polarimetry utilizing a virtually imaged phased array (VIPA) hyperfine spectra disperser.

articleTitle: Power Compensated Bi-Directional Reconfigurable Optical Add/Drop Multiplexer Using Built-In Optical Amplifier
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A power-compensated, bidirectional reconfigurable optical add/drop multiplexer is proposed. The system performance is built on a bidirectional 4 x 2.5 Gb/s 50 km transmission with only 0.2 dB of power penalty compared to unidirectional transmission.

articleTitle: Control of FWM Phase-matching Condition Using the Brillouin Slow Light Effect in Fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: All-optical control of FWM phase-matching condition is demonstrated using the Brillouin slow light effect in optical fibers. A 20 dB variation on the wavelength conversion efficiency has been obtained.

articleTitle: Fast Light Improvement using Periodic Bending of Erbium-Doped Fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This investigation for the first time, experimentally demonstrates the fast light improvement in an erbium-doped fiber. The time advance is increased over 140% by the periodic bending of erbium-doped fiber.

articleTitle: Tailoring of the transmission window in realistic hollow-core Bragg fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A new design with air and silica layer pairs properly combined in the hollow-core Bragg fiber cladding has been proposed, which provides the possibility to tailor the transmission window characteristics.

articleTitle: Characterization of Randomly Varying Birefringence in Long Single Mode Fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report an application of new vector model of fiber Raman amplifier to characterize randomly varying birefringence in long single mode fiber. We find that analysis of the polarization dependent Raman gain can be used for the measurements of beat and birefringence correlation lengths and the polarization mode dispersion value. The results for averaged PMD parameters are consistent with the values obtained by means of the Jones matrix eigenanalysis method.

articleTitle: Experimental Performance Comparison of Duobinary Formats for 40 Gb/s Long-Haul Transmission
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally compare the performance of various types of duobinary modulation formats for 40 Gb/s long-haul transmission. After having measured their respective robustness to accumulation of ASE noise, chromatic dispersion, PMD and intra-channel nonlinear effects, we show that transmission in excess of 2000 km can be envisaged.

articleTitle: Achieving 100G Transmission Rates in Packet Transport Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A new method for scaling packet ring network transmission capacity from 10 Gbits/s to 100 Gbits/s is presented in this article. The concept of high capacity packet rings is introduced as a way of enabling service providers to fully utilize the installed network capacity for the scaling and distribution of high definition IP video services. It describes a hashing mechanism for load balancing and enhanced resiliency over the high capacity links.

articleTitle: Novel NZ-DSF for Submarine Transmission Systems without Discrete Dispersion Compensation
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: NZ-DSF with negative dispersion and negative dispersion slope was realized by restrict mode excitation method. Residual dispersion compensation free submarine cable system is proposed by combination of standard SMF and fabricated fiber.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of High-Rate LDPC Codes for PMD Compensation by Turbo Equalization
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Several LDPC-codes with rate above 0.9 are proposed, and employed in PMD- compensation by LDPC-coded turbo-equalization. The block-circulant LDPC(15328,13893) is only 1.25 dB away from the channel-capacity limit for DGD of 125 ps (and NRZ transmission at 10- Gb/s).

articleTitle: Advanced Repeater Architectures with Ultra-Long Spans for Submarine Systems
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a comparative analysis of two remotely pumped amplifiers schemes used for long-haul transmission. Our numerical and experimental studies show that the remotely pumped EDFA scheme is superior to the Raman assisted EDFA system.

articleTitle: Cost effective OSNR monitor using LC phase shifter
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We have demonstrated an improved Optical Signal to Noise Ratio (OSNR) monitor using Liquid-Crystal (LC) cell phase shifter. The test results show it is a cost effective and practical way to OSNR monitoring.

articleTitle: Ultra-Long Haul Fiber Transmission Technologies and Techniques
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper will describe the main areas of focus of present ultra-long haul transmission research: increased repeater spacing, spectral efficiency, and higher data rates.

articleTitle: Wavelength Meter Based on a Birefringent Medium and a Polarimeter
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A simple technique to measure the frequency drift of monochromatic optical sources based on the polarization change caused by a birefringent material is demonstrated. Preliminary experimental results show a resolution of 0.8 pm.

articleTitle: Optical Path Computation Element interworking with Network Management System for Transparent Mesh Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Optical PCE and its interwork with the NMS were investigated for planning and operation of optical transparent networks. We successfully verified effective and fast optical-path computation taking into account the physical impairments and wavelength continuity.

articleTitle: Hybrid SOA-Raman Amplifiers for Fiber-to-the-Home and Metro Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: SOA-Raman amplifiers have broad gain bandwidth (> 80 nm) and can be designed to operate in any wavelength region compatible with single-mode optical fiber. We review recent progress in SOA-Raman amplified access and metro systems.

articleTitle: SD-WAN : A Technology for the Efficient Use of Bandwidth in Multi-Wavelength Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: SD-WAN technology offers multiple advantages over other networking technologies like EoS, S-EoS and RPR. We conduct theoretical and experimental validation of this technology and propose an application example in the MSO environment.

articleTitle: Development of Cleanliness Specifications for Single-Mode, Angled Physical Contact MT Connectors
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper summarizes the latest research of iNEMI (International Electronics Manufacturing Initiative) on development of cleanliness specification for single-mode angle physical contact MT fiber optics connectors. The acceptance criteria matrix for MT connectors is proposed.

articleTitle: Digital Virtual Concatenation Protocol Enables Super-Wavelength 40G Service Transmission over Trans-Oceanic and High PMD Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Digital Virtual Concatenation allows service transmission of high-bandwidth services over existing WDM infrastructures. Results are presented showing 40Gb/s service transmission over a 2000km link with 65ps peak PMD, and over a 8,477km trans-oceanic network.

articleTitle: The Transition to Metro WDM Optical Meshes
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The most cost effective transport for high bandwidth metro networks uses ROADM enabled DWDM technology, with ring based protection. With appropriate engineering early on, such networks can gracefully and cost effectively evolve to optical meshes.

articleTitle: Bandwidth-Efficient Protection Strategies for Multi-Protected Multi-Service Backbone Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: For backbone IP-over-WDM transport networks, we propose a node-disjoint path protection framework for multi-failure scenarios based on protection tiers plus strategies for backup capacity sharing either employable separately or combinable for significant protection capacity reduction.

articleTitle: Status of Industry Efforts to Deploy EDC and Advanced Modulation Schemes for Extended Reach Transport Applications
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The current status of industrial efforts to standardize interoperable optical interfaces applied to transmitters and receivers is reviewed with particular emphasis on the application of EDC and advanced modulation schemes emerging from OIF/ITU-T targeted transmissions over longer dispersion uncompensated distances.

articleTitle: Laser Linewidth Limitations for Optical Systems with High-Order Modulation Employing Feed Forward Digital Carrier Phase Estimation
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Laser linewidth requirements for optical systems with homodyne detection and feed forward digital phase estimation are determined by extensive Monte Carlo simulations, and shown to be a stringent limitation for high-order modulation formats.

articleTitle: Energy Consumption in Access Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a comparison of energy consumption of access networks. We consider passive optical networks, fiber to the node, point-to-point optical systems and WiMAX. Optical access technologies provide the most energy-efficient solutions.

articleTitle: Evolution to Colorless and Directionless ROADM Architectures
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Broad deployment of ROADMs based on wavelength selective switching has significantly improved optical network flexibility. This paper discusses opportunities to extend upon these advances with colorless and directionless add/drop switching and indicates technology advancements toward this end.

articleTitle: Scalable Extended Reach PON
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Extended reach highly-scalable, fully passive WDM/TDM-PON allows reaching >1000 users along protected 100 km by colorless ONUs, centralized light-generation and control, single-fiber access and remote amplification. ONUs are based on 1.25/2.5/5Gbps-capable RSOA and downstream at 10 Gbps.

articleTitle: 10-Gb/s OFDMA-PON for Delivery of Heterogeneous Services
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a novel method to generate transparent pipes for transmission of heterogeneous services over 10-Gb/s OFDMA-PON architecture. We successfully demonstrated the simultaneous transmission of two PON channels combined with a standard WiMAX channel.

articleTitle: Wide-range, Accurate and Simple Digital Frequency Offset Compensator for Optical Coherent Receivers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a digital frequency offset compensator for optical coherent QPSK receivers. The compensation accuracy reaches ± 30 MHz while the range covers ± 5 GHz. This would realize coherent receivers with common off-the-shelf tunable lasers.

articleTitle: Physical Impairment Based Regenerator Placement and Routing in Translucent Optical Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel constraint-based routing (CBR) algorithm taking into account the dominant linear and nonlinear fiber optical transmission impairments has been analyzed. It is shown that CBR and intelligent regenerator placement decrease the blocking probability significantly.

articleTitle: Optical Packet-Switched WDM Networks: a Cost and Energy Perspective
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A collection of slides from the author's conference presentation on "Optical packet-switched WDM networks: a cost and energy perspective" is given.

articleTitle: Next Generation PON in Emerging Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper presents an overview on the next generation PON techniques in which the developing trends of 10 G EPON, WDM-PON, hybrid WDM/TDM-PON, long-reach PON and PON/RoF convergence are outlined.

articleTitle: A real-time CMA-based 10 Gb/s polarization demultiplexing coherent receiver implemented in an FPGA
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: One advantage of signal-processing based coherent receivers is the ability to polarization-demultiplex in the digital domain. In this paper, we report on an FPGA-based-real-time implementation of a 10 Gb/s receiver with a CMA-based demultiplexer.

articleTitle: Low-Cost and Robust 1-Gbit/s Plastic Optical Fiber Link Based on Light-Emitting Diode Technology
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: 1-Gbit/s transmission is demonstrated over 50 m of step-index PMMA plastic optical fiber (1-mm core-diameter) using a commercial light-emitting diode. This is enabled by use of discrete multitone modulation with up to 64-QAM constellation mapping.

articleTitle: Next Generation FEC for Optical Communication
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A collection of slides from the author's conference presentation is given.

articleTitle: Super-Broadband Optical Wireless Access Technologies
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Network enabling technologies and architectures design for delivering super-broadband wireless services at >1 Gb/s over optical access networks are reviewed. Cost-efficient optical mm-wave generation and transmission technology, optical OFDM, and hierarchical architecture for high-mobility access are discussed.

articleTitle: MAC Protocols for Optical Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiple Access (OFDMA)-based Passive Optical Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel passive optical network (PON) architecture based on optical orthogonal frequency division multiple access (OFDMA) technologies is presented. Two potential medium access control (MAC) methods namely dynamic circuit transmission and fixed burst transmission are investigated.

articleTitle: WSS Switching Engine Technologies
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Various switching engines such as MEMS, liquid crystal, and phased arrays, can be used to implement a colorless WSS. Switching engine affect on device design characteristics and implications on specifications for future applications are discussed.

articleTitle: Multi-rate (100G/40G/10G) Transport Over Deployed Optical Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: In this paper we describe the boundary conditions for upgrading existing 10 G optical transport networks with 40 G and 100 G channels and the operational issues in multi-rate optical networks.

articleTitle: Powering Next Generation Networks by Laser Light over Fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Power over fiber has successfully introduced optical fiber for current measurements in high-voltage electrical networks. The technology is ready to power additional electronic circuitry for network monitoring and restoration in passive, optical fiber communications networks.

articleTitle: Cost Comparison of Networks Using Traditional 10 and 40 Gb/s Transponders Versus OFDM Transponders
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: OFDM allows flexible adjustment of transmission data rate according to channel properties. We propose to use OFDM transponders and calculate the cost at which OFDM networks result in lower CAPEX compared to traditional networks.

articleTitle: Improving Sensitivity and Spectral Efficiency in Direct-Detection Optical OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Analysis and simulations show that boosting the carrier power relative to the sideband just prior to photodetection, using an optical filter, will significantly increase the sensitivity and spectral efficiency of direct-detection optical orthogonal frequency-division multiplexed systems.

articleTitle: Bend and Twist Sensing in a Multiple-Core Optical Fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A method for estimating an optical fiber's shape from internal strain states is presented. Localized sensing of both bending and twisting requires a specialized multi- core fiber design, high-performance static strain sensing, and robust reconstruction algorithms.

articleTitle: 10Gb/s Free-Space Optical Transmission using OFDM
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report the first experimental demonstration of 10 Gb/s free-space optical transmission using orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM). The OFDM system provides superior performance, with a 3 dB improvement in receiver sensitivity over NRZ OOK.

articleTitle: On the Effect of FWM in Coherent Optical OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We derive the channel capacity of CO-OFDM systems limited by FWM. Simulations confirm that Peak-to-Average-Power-Ratio reduction techniques are suitable for FWM mitigation. These techniques can utilize the decreased capacity to significantly increase the system reach.

articleTitle: Perspectives of Radio over Fiber Technologies
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Radio-over-fiber technologies enable efficient provisioning of broadband wireless services both in access and in in-building networks, in particular when combined with flexible optical routing and dispersion-robust RoF transport techniques, such as optical frequency multiplying.

articleTitle: Impact of Polarisation Dependent Loss on Coherent POLMUX-NRZ-DQPSK
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present simulations and measurements on the effect of PDL on a POLMUX-NRZ- DQPSK signal. We show that the orientation between the POLMUX signal and PDL element has a major impact on the OSNR performance.

articleTitle: Large Girth Low-Density Parity-Check Codes for Long-Haul High-Speed Optical Communications
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: An FEC scheme based on large girth LDPC codes is proposed. A girth-10 block-circulant LDPC code of rate 0.8 outperforms its turbo-product code counterpart by 0.95 dB at BER of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-10</sup>, on an AWGN channel. It provides the net effective coding gain of 10.95 dB at BER of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-12</sup>. In long-haul optical transmission at 40-Gb/s it provides at least 1.47 dB improvement over corresponding turbo-product code.

articleTitle: 10 Gbps VCSELs with High Single Mode Output in 1310nm and 1550 nm Wavelength Bands
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A new generation of 10 Gb/s wafer fused VCSELs show high single mode output in excess of 2 mW at 80°C (6 mW at 20°C) in the 1310 nm band and 1.5 mW at 80°C (4 mW at 20°C) in the 1550 nm band. Error free transmission over 10 km of standard single mode fiber was performed with less than 1 dB penalty.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of a Coherently Modulated and Directly Detected Optical OFDM System Using an RF-Tone Insertion
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate an RF-tone assisted OFDM transmission. Our system has a 5-dB better sensitivity compared to the conventional baseband SSB-OFDM and exhibits a negligible penally transmission after 260 km of SSMF.

articleTitle: Digital Signal Processing Options in Long Haul Transmission
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Digital signal processing (DSP) combined with spectrally efficient modulation has redefined the limits for long-haul transmission. We survey the options currently under consideration, including the impact of technology and discuss future directions for DSP research.

articleTitle: All-Optical Polarization Control Through Brillouin Amplification
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Amplification through stimulated Brillouin scattering in optical fibers can totally modify the polarization properties of the light, enabling an all-optical polarization control and a direct estimate on the fiber birefringence.

articleTitle: Field Trial of 160-Gbit/s, Polarization-Division Multiplexed RZ-DQPSK Transmission System using Automatic Polarization Control
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We have successfully demonstrated a field trial of 160-Gbit/s, RZ-DQPSK polarization-division multiplexed transmission system over 214 km using automatic polarization control. Q-factors of the signals have been kept stable for more than five days.

articleTitle: High-Speed Transmission over Multimode Optical Fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Digital modulation techniques that enable high-speed transmission over multimode optical fibers made of silica as well as polymer are discussed. Multilevel modulation provides the potential for high speed short-reach transmission even with low bandwidth components.

articleTitle: Nanophotonic Optical Interconnection Network Architecture for On-Chip and Off-Chip Communications
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: An architecture for an integrated low-power, high-bandwidth optical interconnection network based on microring resonator technology is presented. The layout of the non-blocking network is described and a simulation-based performance evaluation is conducted.

articleTitle: Cost Minimization Planning for Passive Optical Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We plan PON network deployment to minimize its total cost. An efficient heuristic is proposed, which can reduce 50%~70% PON network deployment costs compared to a benchmark sectoring approach.

articleTitle: The Capacity of Fiber-Optic Communication Systems
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a capacity estimate of fiber-optic communication systems limited by fiber nonlinearity. The analysis reveals that a capacity of ~5 bits/s/Hz in a single polarization for transmission over 2000 km is possible using advanced technologies.

articleTitle: 100 Gb/s challenges and solutions
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The article consists of a Powerpoint presentation on 100 Gb/s optical transport network. The areas discussed include: 100 Gb/s transport formats; transmission system design and trade-offs; IP traffic; parallel wavelength approach; serial transport approach; serial modulation; ETDM OOK transmitter; optical duobinary filtering and modulation; optical equalization; BER performance; polarization-multiplexed DQPSK; coherent optical receiver; optical signal-to-noise ratio; chromatic dispersion tolerance; polarization mode dispersion; nonlinear interactions; electronic and opto-electronic components; WDM NRZ transmission; VSB transmission; Ethernet; and spectral efficiency etc. etc.

articleTitle: A 40-Gb/s QSFP Optoelectronic Transceiver in a 0.13μm CMOS Silicon-on-Insulator Technology
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We have demonstrated a 40-Gb/s optoelectronic transceiver in a quad small form-factor pluggable (QSFP) module. Each module includes a 4x10-Gb/s, 0.13 μm CMOS silicon-on-insulator integrated optoelectronic transceiver chip co-packaged with a single, externally modulated CW laser.

articleTitle: Mitigation of Reflection-induced Crosstalk in a WDM Access Network
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Reduction of reflection-induced crosstalk in a link employing Reflective Semiconductor Optical Amplifier achieved by applying Bias Dithering at RSOA and Phase Modulation at the source gives 6dB and 7dB improvement in power penalty, respectively.

articleTitle: Degraded-Service-Aware Multipath Provisioning in Telecom Mesh Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We investigate multipath provisioning in telecom mesh networks. The objectives are to minimize link loads and support degraded service, namely guarantee a fraction of the requested bandwidth even in case of a link failure.

articleTitle: SOA Gate Array Recirculating Buffer for Optical Packet Switching
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A compact recirculating buffer using an InP-based 2×2 switch with gain and a fiber delay line is demonstrated at 40 Gb/s. Packet throughput of 98% is measured for up to 8 circulations, or 0.18 μs.

articleTitle: Transmission of 107-Gb/s DQPSK over Verizon 504-km Commercial LambdaXtreme® Transport System
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A 107-Gb/s field trial was conducted on a traffic carrying long-haul LambdaXtreme® transport platform over an active 504-km Verizon route in Florida thus proving upgradeability to 100 G of the Alcatel-Lucent 50-GHz spaced ULH DWDM system.

articleTitle: PON Evolution from TDMA to WDM-PON
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: WDM-PONs are the next step from today's EPONs/GPONs to accommodate further traffic growth and facilitate new applications. WDM-PON variants are analyzed and proposed as solution for a unified optical access and backhauling network.

articleTitle: Efficient FEC for Optical Communications using Concatenated Codes to Combat Error-floor
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose concatenated LDPC(9252,7967)+RS(992,956) codes for application to systems beyond 40 Gb/s, taking practical implementation into account. Simulation shows that the Q limit is 7.1 dB, and that the concatenation effectively suppresses unwanted error-floor.

articleTitle: PLZT Waveguide Devices for High Speed Switching and Filtering
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: High-speed optical switches were developed in electro-optic (Pb,La)(Zr,Ti)O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (PLZT) waveguides. A 1×2 optical path switch showed <;2.5 ns switching time. An 8×1 wavelength selective switch based on a tunable AWG showed 15 ns switching time.

articleTitle: High-speed 1.1-μm-range InGaAs VCSELs
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We have developed 1.1-μm-range high-speed VCSELs based on InGaAs-QWs for high-speed and highly reliable optical interconnections. 3-dB bandwidth up to 20 GHz and error-free 30-Gbps 100 m operations were demonstrated with oxide confined VCSELs. We also developed buried tunnel junction VCSELs to further improve the relaxation oscillation frequency limit. 3-dB bandwidth up to 24 GHz and error-free 40-Gbps operations were demonstrated with these VCSELs.

articleTitle: Hybrid Integration Technology for High Functionality Devices in Optical Communications
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper reviews the techniques and results for photonic hybrid integration of active semiconductor devices and passive planar waveguides. The paper shows the CIP platform scaleability in terms of cost, performance and complexity of integration.

articleTitle: Optical OFDM - A Candidate for Future Long-Haul Optical Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We review coherent-optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) for long-haul optical transmission systems. Two important aspects of such systems are reviewed: RF-aided phase noise compensation and polarization division multiplexing enabled by MIMO processing.

articleTitle: Resource Provisioning for Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiple Access (OFDMA)-based Virtual Passive Optical Networks (VPON)
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A virtualization mechanism of passive optical networks (PON) based on optical orthogonal frequency division multiple access (OFDMA) technologies is introduced. A comparison between two types of resource provisioning schemes for virtual PON is studied.

articleTitle: Optical Performance Monitoring from FIR Filter Coefficients in Coherent Receivers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a robust and precise optical performance monitoring technique from FIR filter coefficients in coherent receivers with digital equalization. Residual chromatic dispersion, DGD and OSNR are simultaneously estimated from measured 111 Gbit/s data.

articleTitle: Multiplier-free Phase Recovery for Optical Coherent Receivers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a multiplier-free pre-decision phase recovery for optical coherent receivers. The complexity is much lower than previous m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> power phase recovery, while simulation and experiment show that the performance is virtually same.

articleTitle: OFDM: From Copper and Wireless to Optical
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A slide presentation is given on orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) technology both in optical fibre communicationsa and copper wire technology.

articleTitle: 1.5mW/Gbps Low Power Optical Interconnect Transmitter Exploiting High-Efficiency VCSEL and CMOS Driver
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a low power optical interconnect transmitter which employs a 990 nm VCSEL with high efficiency and low threshold current, and a 130 nm CMOS driver. The power dissipated by the transmitter is 15.1 mW at 10 Gbps.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration for Delivering 1-Gb/s OFDM Signals over 80-km SSMF in 40-GHz Radio-over-Fiber Access Systems
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally show the first demonstration of a super-broadband radio-over-fiber system transmitting 1-Gb/s OFDM signals on 40-GHz millimeter-wave carriers. It is achieved over 80-km SSMF without dispersion compensation with less than 0.5-dB power penalty at BER of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>.

articleTitle: PMD Insensitive Direct-Detection Optical OFDM Systems Using Self-Polarization Diversity
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Novel self-polarization diversity without dynamic polarization control is proposed to compensate PMD in direct-detection optical OFDM systems. We show that PMD impairments are virtually completely eliminated in the optical OFDM system using this technique.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of 340 km SSMF Transmission Using a Virtual Single Sideband OFDM Signal that Employs Carrier Suppressed and Iterative Detection Techniques
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a virtual SSB-OFDM with direct detection that uses half the electrical bandwidth by employing an RF tone at the edge of the signal. We transmit 10 Gbps data with a 4-QAM over 340 km of SSMF with no penalty.

Index Terms: Optical Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing Signal

articleTitle: Silicon Photonics: A Low Cost Integration Platform for Datacom and Telecom Applications
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Si photonics technology as a platform for the realization of cost effective products for telecom and datacom applications is reviewed and recent progress in the area is reported.

articleTitle: Demonstration of All-Optical Multi-Wavelength Message Routing for Silicon Photonic Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate all-optical switching of 20 wavelength channels simultaneously in a silicon broadband comb switch, and perform single-channel BER measurements through both ports. A statistical characterization of the insertion loss and extinction ratio is included.

articleTitle: Direction-Independent Add/Drop Access for Multi-Degree ROADMs
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We analyze system costs and associated tradeoffs for implementing direction- independent add/drop access for multi-degree ROADMs employing 1×K wavelength selective switches (WSS) and 3D-MEMS-based mirror array switches.

articleTitle: Extended Reach GPON Using High Gain Semiconductor Optical Amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A 1300 nm semiconductor optical amplifier has been developed for extended reach GPON applications. The high gain of 29 dB has and enabled a commercial GPON system to operate over 60 km and with 128-way split.

articleTitle: Large-Scale Photonic Integrated Circuit Transmitters with Monolithically Integrated Semiconductor Optical Amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We have successfully demonstrated large-scale photonic integrated circuit (LS-PIC) transmitters with monolithically integrated semiconductor optical amplifiers. Data is presented for for 10 channel devices operating at 10 and 40 Gb/sec.

articleTitle: Demonstration of RSOA-based WDM PON Operating at Symmetric Rate of 1.25 Gb/s with High Reflection Tolerance
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate an RSOA-based WDM PON operating at the symmetric rate of 1.25 Gb/s by using a low-frequency subcarrier (2.5 GHz). The performance is robust against the remodulation noise as well as the reflection noise.

articleTitle: Efficient Wavelength Conversion Using Triangular Pulses Generated Using a SuperStructured Fiber Bragg Grating
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The generation of picosecond triangular optical pulses is experimentally demonstrated using SSFBG technology. This shape provides a more than two-fold improvement in the performance of a wavelength-conversion scheme based on self-phase-modulation in fiber and offset-filtering.

articleTitle: Chip-to-chip board-level optical data buses
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We have demonstrated 160-Gb/s bidirectional optical data buses using parallel optical transceivers with 16-transmitter plus 16-receiver 10-Gb/s channels on optical printed circuit boards with 32 polymer waveguides, providing requisite technologies for chip-to-chip board-level optical interconnects.

articleTitle: 300-Gb/s, 24-Channel Full-Duplex, 850-nm, CMOS-Based Optical Transceivers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report a compact, low-profile transceiver with 24 transmitter and 24 receiver channels, each operating at 12.5 Gb/s. The achieved 300 Gb/s aggregate bi-directional data rate is the highest ever reported for parallel optical modules.

articleTitle: Reflection tolerance of RSOA-based WDM PON
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We investigate the effects of back-reflection in RSOA-based WDM PON utilizing the remodulation technique. The downstream signal is likely to have severe reflection tolerance (-42 ~ -35 dB), which highly depends on the RSOA gain.

articleTitle: Experimental Realisation of 3 × 3 MIMO System with Mode Group Diversity Multiplexing Limited by Modal Noise
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We show experimentally the feasibility of a 3×3 MIMO system based on Mode Group Diversity Multiplexing over GI-MMF. The main limiting effect of modal noise is reduced by large detection areas.

articleTitle: Efficient, Fault-Tolerant All-Optical Multicast Networks via Network Coding
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Network coding, an emerging field of research, provides a means to create efficient all-optical multicast networks that feature hitless reconfiguration. Here a photonic bitwise exclusive-OR hardware element supplies the key enabling functionality.

articleTitle: Fiber Distribution of Local Oscillator for Atacama Large Millimeter Array
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The ALMA photonic reference is a tunable, phase-stable local oscillator (LO) reference for a radio astronomy array. The LO is 27-122 GHz, actively phase corrected, and distributed on 15-km of fiber.

articleTitle: Requirements for Bend Insensitive Fibers for Verizon's FiOS and FTTH applications
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Escalating bandwidth requirements (video, data, and voice) for residential customers has justified the fiber penetration into buildings and living units. To achieve efficient installations of fiber cables, many challenges in existing optical fiber design must be overcome. Macro-bend loss was identified as a major barrier for fiber deployment in such small, dense and tight scenarios, in which copper was typically the choice. In this paper, we present a detailed analysis of the requirements for macro-bend performance, and the results of field trails using revolutionary fiber technology.

articleTitle: 30 Gbit/s RZ-8-PSK Transmission over 2800 km Standard Single Mode Fibre without Inline Dispersion Compensation
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: For the first time, 30-Gbit/s-RZ-8-PSK (including FEC overhead) transmission over 2800 km standard single mode fibre without inline compensation of chromatic dispersion is experimentally demonstrated using homodyne detection, carrier phase estimation and electronic dispersion compensation.

articleTitle: Hitless-Reconfigurable and Bandwidth-Scalable Silicon Photonic Circuits for Telecom and Interconnect Applications
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We describe silicon microring-resonator-based microphotonic circuits that support complete (amplitude and phase) disabling of resonant states, enabling novel capabilities: truly- hitless switching/tuning of high-order, telecom-grade channel add-drop filters, dispersionless FSR multiplication, and "hot-swapping" of photonic subsystems.

articleTitle: DQPSK modulation for robust optical transmission
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The feasibility of long-haul transmission using differential quadrature phase shift keying (DQPSK) modulation is discussed. We focus in particular on the trade-off between spectral efficiency and reach in optical transmission systems using DQPSK modulation.

articleTitle: WDM-PON Systems Using Cross-Remodulation to Double Network Capacity with Reduced Rayleigh Scattering Effects
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A simple WDM-PON architecture operating at two wavelength bands is demonstrated to increase the system capacity and suppress the Rayleigh scattering effect on the remodulated upstream signals. The system adds minimal extra components and loss.

articleTitle: Channel-by-channel tunable optical dispersion compensator consisting of arrayed-waveguide grating and liquid crystal on silicon
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a tunable optical dispersion compensator consisting of an arrayed-waveguide grating and a liquid crystal on silicon. We obtained a tuning range of ± 800 ps/nm with a bandwidth of 16 GHz.

articleTitle: Determination of the impact of a quality of transmission estimator margin on the dimensioning of an optical network
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The impact of the quality of transmission estimator margin on the prediction accuracy for a connection establishment in network planning is studied as a function of the knowledge of the actual chromatic dispersion map.

articleTitle: Ultra-Fast Adaptive Digital Polarization Control in a Realtime Coherent Polarization-Multiplexed QPSK Receiver
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A digital polarization control system integrated in a 2.8 Gbit/s realtime polarization-multiplexed coherent QPSK system compensates for endless polarization changes having a maximum gradient of 3.5 krad/s (12 krad/s) with 1 dB (3.9 dB) loss in receiver sensitivity.

articleTitle: MIMO radio signals over fiber in picocells for increased WLAN coverage
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We show that separating base station antennas in an optically-fed 2×3 MIMO WLAN system increases the overall coverage area in picocells. A peak throughput of 130 Mb/s was measured for antenna spacings of both 16 cm and 7 m.

articleTitle: 100 Gbit/s All-Optical OFDM Transmission Using 4 × 25 Gbit/s Optical Duobinary Signals with Phase-Controlled Optical Sub-Carriers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper proposes 100-Gbit/s optical-OFDM transmission using the ODB format. An OFDM signal generated using a simple multi-carrier generator and multi-carrier modulator is successfully transmitted over a 20-km SMF and 100-km DSF without dispersion compensation.

articleTitle: OCDM-based Photonic Encryption with Provable Security
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We introduce two novel techniques, random noise on unused channels and varying the inter-code phases on realistic framing repetition, to obtain an OCDM-based encryption scheme for which we can prove desirable security guarantees.

articleTitle: Enhancing Backward Recursive PCE-based Computation (BRPC) for Inter-Domain Protected LSP Provisioning
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A PCE-based scheme exploiting BRPC and PCEP extensions is proposed for computing protected LSPs in multi-domain networks. Experimental evaluation shows that the proposed scheme is effective in terms of traffic engineering solution and protocol efficiency.

articleTitle: Polarization-multiplexed 1 Gsymbol/s, 128 QAM (14 Gbit/s) coherent optical transmission over 160 km using a 1.4 GHz Nyquist filter
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We have transmitted a polarization-multiplexed 1-Gsymbol/s, 128 QAM (14-Gbit/s) coherent optical signal over 160 km using a 1.4-GHz Nyquist filter. A heterodyne technique was used between a frequency-stabilized C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> laser and high-speed local oscillator.

articleTitle: Optical Distribution of OFDM and Impulse-Radio UWB in FTTH networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Proposal, experimental demonstration and performance comparison of impulse-radio UWB and OFDM UWB distribution in FTTH networks for high-definition audio/video broadcasting is presented. OFDM-UWB exhibits better performance compared with its impulse- radio counterpart with better spectral efficiency.

articleTitle: Cladding-Pumped Yb-Doped Solid Photonic Bandgap Fiber for ASE Suppression in Shorter Wavelength Region
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate suppression of amplified spontaneous emission at 1030 nm in a cladding-pumped ytterbium-doped solid photonic bandgap fiber. This fiber should play an important role for a high power fiber laser lasing around 1180 nm.

articleTitle: Network Cost Savings from Router Bypass in IP over WDM Core Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Optimization of IP and WDM network architecture using IP router link bypass provides cost savings in both layers. Results indicate that optimal level of router bypass varies with total traffic volume and router interface speed.

articleTitle: Comparison of OOK- and PAM-4 Modulation for 10 Gbit/s Transmission over up to 300 m Polymer Optical Fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: 10 Gbit/s Transmission over up to 300 m of multimode 62.5 μm core-diameter perfluorinated graded-index polymer optical fiber is compared using on-off-keying (OOK) or 4-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM-4) and feed-forward or decision-feedback equalization.

articleTitle: Coherent Detection in Long-Haul Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We review the potentials and challenges of applying coherent detection in long-haul transmission systems. We compare several different coherent detection schemes from the aspects of receiver sensitivity, carrier phase recovery, and fiber nonlinearity induced penalty.

articleTitle: A 10.3 Gbit/s LAN-PHY based Burst-mode Transmitter with a fast 6 ns turn-on/off time for 10 Gbps-based PON Systems
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel 10.3 Gbit/s LAN-PHY based burst-mode transmitter with a fast 6 ns turn-on/off time and a high launch power more than +3.3 dBm over the temperature range 0 to 70 degree-C was successfully demonstrated by using a new impedance-controlled DC-coupled burst-mode LD driver circuit.

articleTitle: A Self-Survivable WDM-PON Architecture with Centralized Wavelength Monitoring, Protection and Restoration for both Upstream and Downstream Links
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A centrally-controlled, bi-directional WDM-PON architecture has been demonstrated. The self- survivable scheme can protect all types of failures in distribution and feeder fibers, remote nodes, and transmitters in CO and ONUs.

articleTitle: Coherent Optical OFDM Systems Using Self Optical Carrier Extraction
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a new coherent optical OFDM system architecture using self optical carrier extraction. It requires simplified DSP at the coherent receiver. The system shows good tolerance to phase noise, laser linewidth, and fiber nonlinearity.

articleTitle: Expanding network applications with coherent detection
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The practical domain of network applications is expanded by the use of coherent receivers and comprehensive equalization. This includes line equipment reduction, channel spectral efficiency design, network spectral efficiency design, reclaim of PMD compromised fiber plant, and capacity evolution at fixed line design. Attendant to these capabilities are new design considerations such as valuable and of FEC overhead, polarization dependent losses, dispersion, and phase noise. Coherent optical transmission will be preeminent in high capacity optical networking.

articleTitle: Flexible 10 Gbps, 8-user DPSK-OCDMA System with 16×16 Ports Encoder and 16-level Phase-shifted SSFBG Decoders
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: 16-chip, 16-level phase-shifted superstructured fiber Bragg grating (SSFBG) encoder/decoder is reported for the first time. 10 Gbps, 8-user optical code-division-multiple- access system has been demonstrated using hybrid 16x16 ports encoder/SSFBG decoder.

articleTitle: Generation of Carrier Suppressed Optical mm-wave Signals using Frequency Quadrupling and no Optical Filtering
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This work demonstrates a novel mm-wave generation using a frequency quadrupling technique. Only one external MZM is used and no optical filter is needed. It provides a simple and inexpensive choice for WDM RoF applications.

articleTitle: Hybrid TDM-WDM EPON Repeater
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We have proposed a hybrid TDM-WDM EPON repeater aggregating 16 EPONs with single fiber, and have experimentally confirmed that an extended power budget of more than 20 dB is achievable with no performance degradation.

articleTitle: Photonic Bandgap Fiber for New Wavelength Range
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Recent progress on silica-based photonic bandgap fiber technologies are reviewed aiming at a new wavelength region that includes the visible, ultraviolet, and infrared regions. Possible optical active devices at hereto unused wavelengths are discussed.

articleTitle: Manipulation of Photons by 2D and 3D Photonic Crystals
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The author gives a slide presentation on light photon manipulation by 2D and 3D photonic crystals.

articleTitle: Highly Nonlinear Fibers for Ultrahigh-speed Optical Signal Processing
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Performance of recently developed highly nonlinear fibers is discussed, focusing on application to ultrahigh-speed optical signal processing. Demonstrations of ultrahigh-speed applications using highly nonlinear fibers are also discussed.

articleTitle: OSNR Monitoring Technique for DPSK/DQPSK Signals Based on Self-Heterodyne Detection
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report a new OSNR monitoring method of DPSK/DQPSK signals, which analyzes the RF spectrum obtained by the self-heterodyne detection. The performance of this technique is not affected by the polarization scrambling or fiber dispersion (both CD and PMD).

articleTitle: Dynamic tuning of a supercontinuum using an acoustic grating - experimental and numerical investigation
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We investigate dynamic shaping of the spectrum of a supercontinuum using a tunable acoustic long-period fiber grating filter. We demonstrate reconfigurable spectral enhancement, which is easily tuned by adjustment of an external radio frequency source.

articleTitle: The Optimized Architecture for Transition to All Packet Transport
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We compared three architectures for the performance and cost analysis. We found out in the transaction from TDM to all packet transport, the most reliable and cost effective architecture is the hybrid switch architecture.

articleTitle: Applicability Investigation of Ethernet OAM in Wide Area Network
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Applicability of linktrace and delay measurement functions of Ethernet OAM is investigated. We successfully demonstrate the monitoring scheme of logical topology and change of LAG configurations with the Ethernet OAM functionalities in the wide area network.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable all-optical byte recognition for 40-Gb/s phase-shift-keyed transmission using a planar-lightwave-circuit passive correlator
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate all-optical recognition of byte patterns embedded in phase-shift-keyed data streaming at 40 Gb/s. We use matched filtering to generate an autocorrelation pulse indicating the pattern matching. Matched filtering is implemented using a reconfigurable silica planar-lightwave-circuit optical delay-line filter. We show excellent discrimination against spurious patterns consistent with the theoretical predictions.

articleTitle: Bit Rate Transparent Optical Burst Switching with Contention Resolving Wavelength Conversion
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Optical burst switching using fast, bit-rate transparent switches is presented. Random contention is handled without using optical memory by wavelength conversion. We demonstrate error-free 10 and 40Gb/s burst contention resolution in a 5×5 node prototype.

articleTitle: Applications of Pulse Shaping in High Power Fiber Laser Systems
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The article consists of a Powerpoint presentation on applications of pulse shaping in high power fiber laser systems.
