The paper concludes that many technologies now available for shaping light in fibre, supplemented by an increasing array of fiberised components; leverage of telecom technology and concepts into new and emerging fields represents an important enabler allowing shaping on ns, ps and fs timescales; shaping at high power levels particularly attractive for a host of scientific and industrial processing applications and shaping of the spatial mode profile represents an interesting further source control possibility.

articleTitle: Optical Power Transient Suppression by a Dynamic Broadband Attenuator Based on the Raman Effect
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: An optical attenuator based on the Raman effect is presented which is shown to provide dynamic and broadband suppression of channel power transients in WDM transmission systems, without affecting the normal operation mode.

articleTitle: Accurate modal analysis of microstructured optical fibers with the boundary integral method
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A boundary integral method for calculating leaky and guided modes of microstructured optical fibers is presented. The method is rapidly converging and can handle a large number of inclusions with arbitrary geometries.

articleTitle: Increasing Robustness of Protection Schemes
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Use of intelligent wait-to-restore for reducing the time that circuits are on protect while also reducing the amount of switch-toggling in the network. This paper also proposes a new reporting scheme to reduce isolation time.

articleTitle: Impact of linewidth on system impairment caused by backreflection in WDM PONs
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper experimentally investigates the impact of linewidth on system impairment in WDM-PONs for various wavelength-independent ONU configurations. We show that the power penalty decreases and the optimal ONU gain changes as the linewidth increases.

articleTitle: Fiber Lasers for Frequency Standards in Optical Communications
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Optical light with millihertz relative frequency stabilities and subfemtosecond timing jitter can be produced from stabilized cw or mode-locked fiber lasers. We will discuss the generation, fiber-optic distribution and some applications of these coherent sources.

articleTitle: PMD Compensation at Ultra-High Bit Rates or Optical Spectral Processing All-Order PMD Technology: Compensation, Sensing, Emulation
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A collection of slides from the author's conference presentation on PMD compensation at ultra-high bit rates and optical spectral processing all-order PMD technology is given.

articleTitle: Self-induced fast light in optical fibers using stimulated Brillouin scattering without any pump sources
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a method for realizing pulse advancement induced by stimulated Brillouin scattering in optical fibers without any pump sources. A pulse advancement of 13.65 ns is achieved with this self-induced fast light method.

articleTitle: A novel transmitter based on orthogonal modulation schemes for future passive optical networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A low-cost technique for the upgrade of access passive optical networks based on multitone frequency shift keying (FSK) modulation format combined with conventional intensity modulation is proposed and numerically evaluated.

articleTitle: Ultra-broadband acousto-optic coupling in hole-assisted fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Ultra-broadband acousto-optic coupling is realized by using hole-assisted fiber with flattened beat length characteristics. The coupling bandwidth reaches 120 nm, and can be controlled by designing the air hole structure.

articleTitle: Flexibly tunable multiwavelength erbium-doped fiber laser using dispersion-shifted fiber and digital micromirror device
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report a tunable multiwavelength erbium-doped fiber laser incorporating dispersion-shifted fiber and digital micromirror device. The flexible allocation of wavelengths is achieved by controlling micromirrors. Up to 13 channels with 0.8 nm spacing are generated.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Analog-to-Digital Conversion Using Spatial-Spectral Holography
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Proof-of-concept demonstrations for an optical approach to broadband analog-to-digital conversion are shown with 800 MHz bandwidth and >26 dB dynamic range. Models suggest that this frequency-domain stretched processor could achieve 10-bit performance over 20 GHz bandwidths.

articleTitle: Monolithic Integration of GaAs/AlGaAs Phase Modulator and Photodetector for RF Photonics
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report the design and monolithic fabrication of phase modulator and photodetectors for RF photonics. We demonstrate phase modulation efficiency of 270°V<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, and a bandwidth of 18 GHz. Photodetectors response time is measured to be 8ps.

articleTitle: Dynamic Range of Wavelength Exchange in Highly Nonlinear Dispersion-Shifted Fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We investigate the signal dynamic range of wavelength exchange using 10 Gb/s 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">31</sup>- 1 PRBS. Data exchanging between two wavelengths is achieved with signal dynamic range ~20 dB. Bit-error-rate of <;10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup> is maintained with power penalties of <; 2 dB.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of downloading speed on token-passing based PON system
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We have analyzed performance of the PON system adopting token passing for achieving high downloading speed. A virtue of the token passing has been revealed by numerical calculations.

articleTitle: Costs per Home Connected: The Impacts of Automated Fiber Management On Fiber-to-the-Home Deployments
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate the economic impact of automated fiber management (AFM) in FTTH networks, specifically to defer capital costs and reduce operating costs by automating testing, provisioning, maintenance, troubleshooting, and grooming operations.

articleTitle: Multiwavelength Raman fiber ring lasers with continuous wavelength spacing tunability
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We investigate a flexibly tunable multiwavelength Raman fiber ring laser with continuous wavelength spacing tunability and a high SNR of more than -45 dB incorporating a superimposed chirped fiber Bragg grating.

articleTitle: Undersea Communication Systems Without System Specific Optical Amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrated that a mix of high- and low-gain amplifiers instead of the traditional span loss matched amplifiers can be used in undersea transmission systems without any performance penalty over transoceanic distances.

articleTitle: All-fiber wavelength tunable and mode convertible bandpass filter for optical inter-connections
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report an all-fiber wavelength tunable bandpass filter with multi-mode to single-mode converting property via serially concatenated structure of a helicoidal long-period fiber grating (HLPFG), a hollow optical fiber (HOF), and a multimode fiber (MMF).

articleTitle: Storage Area Network Extension over Passive Optical Networks Using Parallel Signal Detection
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a novel storage passive optical network (PON), which delivers broadband data as well as storage services to the end users through the employment of subcarrier modulation and parallel signal detection (PSD). Experimental results show that the proposed storage PON is capable of providing Gigabit level data and storage transmission in the access network.

articleTitle: Visible Continuum Generation Using a Femtosecond Erbium-Doped Fiber Laser and a Hybrid HNLF-PCF Nonlinear Fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Visible supercontinuum in the fundamental mode is generated in a silica hybrid nonlinear fiber using a femtosecond, erbium-doped fiber laser pump. The nonlinear fiber consists of highly nonlinear, germano-silicate fiber (HNLF) fusion spliced to a photonic crystal fiber (PCF).

articleTitle: OFDM signal transmission by direct modulation of a doped fiber external cavity semiconductor laser
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A doped fiber external cavity laser (DFECL) exhibits high power, narrow linewidth and stable wavelength which may be tuned. We demonstrate IEEE 802.11 signal transmission by direct modulating the ultra long DFECL at ~2.5GHz.

articleTitle: Advances in Amplification Technology for the Agile Optical Network
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The evolution of optical amplifier technology and functionality are described, as designs have merged with novel network functionality and requirements of the Agile optical network.

articleTitle: Impact of Nonlinear Broadening on the Optimal Characteristics of High-Power P2O5-doped Fibre Lasers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The impact of intra-cavity Stokes wave broadening on the performance of P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>-doped fibre lasers is investigated. It is shown that nonlinear broadening of the radiation strongly affects laser performance and optimal configuration of the cavity.

articleTitle: Grating Enhanced Continuum Generation
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We describe the large spectral enhancements that are observed when a continuum is generated in a fiber Bragg grating, and review their use in applications such as frequency metrology that benefit from broadband, spectrally tailored sources.

articleTitle: Precise and simple group delay measurement of dispersive devices based on ultrafast optical differentiation
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a very simple technique for accurately measuring the group delay of dispersive devices. It only requires an optical differentiator (uniform long-period fiber grating), a pulsed laser source and a high-speed oscilloscope.

articleTitle: A Transition Matrix Analysis of the Hinge Model
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We adapt the transition matrix procedure to time-dependent effects in communication systems and subsequently calculate the outage-time statistics resulting from polarization mode dispersion (PMD) in the hinge model.

articleTitle: Optimize operational bandwidth through core design in air-core photonic bandgap fibers for IR transmission
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We determine the optimal inner glass ring thickness and its dependence on the glass index in infrared PBGFs. We find that the optimal thickness is 0.04Λ and the optimal index is as small as possible.

articleTitle: Engineering Availability in a Carrier Ethernet Network
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper presents a method for calculating the availability of a carrier Ethernet network, and describes how to control and design network availability. It evaluates the availability of various carrier Ethernet network architectures with increasing protection, using actual reliability data, to understand the effects of redundancy at different places in the network. The paper explores these concepts and develops a relationship between cost and availability, numerically presenting the cost-versus-protection dynamic. This relationship can be concisely expressed as dollars per nine of availability and subsequently used in the development and deployment of cost-efficient Ethernet networks.

articleTitle: Iterative Equalization and FEC Decoding in Optical Communication Systems: Concepts and Performance
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: MLSE and turbo equalization with convolutional and LDPC codes in presence of PMD channels and outer RS codes are compared. Optimized LDPC codes reduce the gap to information theoretic bounds to the order of ldB.

articleTitle: Field Installable LC Connector for Cables
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper describes the development of the field installable LC connector for Kevlar reinforced cables, with a novel and easy way of terminating Kevlar to maintain good mechanical strength performance.

articleTitle: Time-Multiplexed Photonically-Enabled Radio-Frequency Arbitrary Waveforms with 10-GHz Update Rate
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: For the first time to our knowledge, radio-frequency arbitrary waveforms are reported with 10 GHz waveform update rate by integrating wavelength switching, optical frequency comb generation and spectral line-by-line shaping.

articleTitle: Er3+-doped fluorophosphate glass fiber with ultra low nonlinearity for suppressing four-wave-mixing in L-band EDFA
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We developed Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>-doped fluorophosphate glass fiber with low nonlinearity. With an L-band EDFA employing the fiber the four-wave-mixing crosstalk was 10 dB less than when employing an Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>-doped silica fiber with low nonlinearity.

articleTitle: ASE Noise Instability Migration in WSS ROADM Based Closed Amplified Ring Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We address the ASE noise instability issues in closed ring networks consisted by MEMs based WSS ROADMs. Instabilities in 5 node based optical ring network are experimentally demonstrated and migrated using noise filtering.

articleTitle: Bandgap splitting in liquid crystal photonic bandgap fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The polarization dependent bandgap splitting for nematic liquid crystal photonic bandgap fibers (LCPBGFs) is investigated. We proposed two orthogonal polarization dependent bandgap for guiding linear-polarized fiber modes of LCPBGFs.

articleTitle: PMD Assisted Pump to Signal Noise Transfer in Distributed Fiber Raman Amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a theoretical analysis on the PMD assisted pump to signal noise transfer in distributed fiber Raman amplifiers. New noise mechanisms are pointed out, and their impacts on the system performance are then analyzed.

articleTitle: Inner cladding fiber interferometer for the simultaneous measurement of temperature and strain
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose an inner cladding fiber interferometer formed with a long-period fiber grating pair, which is insensitive to the external contact. We simultaneously measure temperature and strain by separating the grating-free-region and the grating region.

articleTitle: Free-Space Decoy-State Quantum Key Distribution
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Quantum cryptography, the only method which can provide quantifiable security of a distributed key, became the first application of quantum information methods. Complementary to fiber based systems, free space optics enables one to establish a secure key in various new scenarios, e.g., authentication to money machines or short distance links in metropolitan areas. Here we report on secure communication over 144 km between the islands of Tenerife and La Palma. Decoy state analysis ensured the security of our attenuated pulse scheme for a link efficiency of about 35 dB and resulted in key rates of 231 bit/s, clearly demonstrating the feasibility of free space links to satellites enabling global secure key exchange.

articleTitle: Regenerative Properties of 10 Gb/s SOA-DI Wavelength Converter With Practical Pulse Widths
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The regenerative properties are investigated for a wavelength converter designed for practical pulse widths. It is better able to cope with a reduction in the optical signal-to-noise ratio than waveform distortion due to residual dispersion.

articleTitle: State Space Model for TDM-PON Bandwidth Allocation
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a state space model to tackle the bandwidth allocation issue of time division multiplexed passive optical networks (TDM-PONs). It describes the TDM-PON system as a threesome of on-line traffic load, bandwidth arbitration decision, as well as queue status. Analytical results show that this model provides a platform to evaluate performance of diverse bandwidth allocation algorithms.

articleTitle: High-Repetition-Rate Pulsed-Pump Optical Parametric Amplification in Silicon Waveguides
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The net parametric gain evolution inside the silicon waveguides for high speed optical communications is investigated. Pulsed-pump parametric amplification can be a chip-scale solution for high bit rate DWDM systems with pulse width <;1 ps.

articleTitle: Widely Tunable Surface-Relief Bragg Gratings in Polymer Waveguide with Low Power Consumption
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A polymer waveguide Bragg grating was fabricated with non-contact phase-mask. By employing the silicon trench below the grating segment, it was able to tune the wavelengths over 30 nm at a rate of-0.28 nm/mW.

articleTitle: A fiber acousto-optic tunable bandpass filter on high-polarization-splitting fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report on the acousto-optic interaction in a newly developed high-polarization-splitting fiber designed to lift the degeneracy of its cladding modes and on an all-fiber acousto-optic tunable bandpass filters based on this fiber.

articleTitle: Non Inverting and Non Filtered Wavelength Converter Based on an InAs/InP(100) QD Ring Laser at 1.55μm
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel wavelength conversion concept based on InAs/InP(100) quantum-dot ring- laser structure is demonstrated requiring no external laser, optical inversion or optical filtering. Demonstration at 622 Mb/s for a 2 mm ring, suggests applicability for much higher speeds.

articleTitle: On the Statistics of Intra-Channel Four-Wave Mixing in Phase-Modulated Systems
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The correlation functions of intra-channel four-wave mixing (IFWM) in phase-modulated systems are studied. Implementing a phase noise predictor derived from the correlation functions results in a 1 dB improvement for typical terrestrial links.

articleTitle: Microresonators for Photonic Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: High-Q, low loss microdisks vertically coupled to buried bus waveguides were designed and fabricated using selective area deep etching with multi-level masks. The technology combines low loss waveguides with the ability to integrate active functionalities.

articleTitle: Stimulated Brillouin Scattering in F-Doped Optical Fibers and Its Dependences on Strain and Temperature
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Our study proves that F-doped fibers have almost the same Brillouin gain-coefficient as that of GeO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-doped fibers. The sensitivity of acoustic resonance frequency on strain/temperature shows a dependence on fluorine-concentration opposite to that on germanium-concentration.

articleTitle: Time-Slotted Full-Duplex Access Network for Baseband and 60-GHz Millimeter-Wave-Band Radio-over-Fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a time-slotted full-duplex access network for 1.5-Gbps baseband signals and 155Mbps 60-GHz-band radio-over-fiber. A reflective semiconductor optical amplifier at the access point is used to erasure the downlink signal for uplink reutilization purposes.

articleTitle: Technologies for 40 Gb/s and 100Gb/s transmission
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Technology trends of high capacity transmission system together with node and device technologies are summarized that support exploding traffic demand in next generation broadband networks combining telecom and broadcast arena.

articleTitle: DPSK Data Quality Dependencies in Microring-Based Transmitter and Receiver
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Ultra-small DPSK (de)modulators at 10 Gb/s, using silicon-based microrings, are proposed. Data quality of the microring-based DPSK is greatly dependent on operation conditions that can be optimized to improve eye-opening by up-to-7-dB.

articleTitle: Propagation analysis of an 80-Gb/s wavelength-converted signal utilizing XPM
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We model the propagation of an 80-Gb/s wavelength-converted signal generated by utilizing XPM in a highly nonlinear fiber. After propagation over 1280 km or less, wavelength conversion adds no signal degradation in terms of BER.

articleTitle: Wavelength-Insensitive Tap Waveguide Using Mach-Zehnder Structures on Silicon-on-insulator Platform
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A wavelength-insensitive tap waveguide using a relative phase shift between two directional couplers was demonstrated to get 3.7% coupling ratio and 0.25 dB chromaticity across the whole C-band via 12 μm thick silicon-on-insulator waveguide.

articleTitle: Characterizing the Noise Transfer Properties of an All-Optical Regenerator
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: To determine the noise transfer properties of all-optical regenerators, the relative standard deviation for the peak power of the output pulse is shown to be a useful quantity that is consistent with more detailed measurements.

articleTitle: Histogram-Based Bit Error Ratio Estimator for Differential Modulation Formats
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A histogram-based BER estimation method for differential modulation formats is analyzed. It is shown that this BER estimation approach yields more accurate results than conventional extrapolation methods with less simulated symbols.

articleTitle: Dynamics of room temperature DC-induced second-order nonlinearity in poled fiber under an external field
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We investigated room-temperature dynamics of an internal field-induced second-order nonlinearity (SON) in a poled fiber subject to an external DC field (±1.1MV/cm), and obtained an internal SON of ~0.01pm/V with a time constant of ~20s.

articleTitle: Core Network Design and Planning: Challenges and Technology Trend
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The next generation network architectures are inherently related to packet transport and Ethernet technology. In this presentation authors will discuss various technologies and review existing issues in packet aware networks based on optical technology.

articleTitle: Phase-Sensitive Detection for Lossy Ring and Cavity-based Sensors
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Phase-sensitive detection and maximum-phase design provide optimum sensitivity for sensors employing infinite impulse response filters. Practical tradeoffs in the modulation frequency are discussed, and the maximum-phase condition is shown to be advantageous over critically-coupled designs.

articleTitle: Clock Extraction from NRZ-DPSK Signal Using NRZ-DPSK to RZ-OOK Converter Based on Cascaded Long-Period Fiber Grating
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Clock extraction from 10-Gb/s NRZ-DPSK signal using a cascaded long-period fiber grating is experimentally demonstrated. The resultant clock has low timing jitter of <;1 ps. The method is easily applicable up to 640-Gb/s.

articleTitle: Impact of 3R wavelength converter tunability on WDM networks with finite signal impairment threshold
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The effects of 3R wavelength converters (3R-WC) tunability on WDM networks with finite signal impairment threshold are presented. We find that 3R-WCs with limited tuning range can give the same network performance with full tunability.

articleTitle: Wide Band Single Polarization and Polarization Maintaining Fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a new fiber structure using both stress rods and air holes for making wide band single polarization fibers as well as polarization maintaining fibers, and illustrate the results through finite element modeling.

articleTitle: Measurement of First- to Fourth-Order Polarization Mode Dispersion in Optical Fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A high-order polarization mode dispersion technique is proposed to perform the first- to fourth-order PMD measurement. It is experimentally demonstrated to be far more accurate in high-order PMD measurement than the conventional Mueller matrix method.

articleTitle: 10Gbps-80km Transmission by 100GHz-spacing, 8-channel Wavelength-tunable 1.55-μm InGaAlAs Electro-absorption Modulator Integrated DFB Laser
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: 10-Gbps, 80-km transmission was achieved by a wavelength-tunable EA/DFB laser with 8-channels and 100-GHz spacing. A dynamic extinction ratio over 10-dB and a power penally below 2-dB were achieved over 5.6-nm continuous wavelength tuning range.

articleTitle: Opto-Electronic Phase-Locked Loop using Adhered-Ridge-Waveguide Periodically-Poled Lithium Niobate for High-Bit-Rate Clock Recovery
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: New experimental results support optoelectronic PLLs, incorporating PPLN adhered- ridge-waveguide, for high-bit-rate clock recovery. Sub-clock extraction and synchronization of a 40-GHz and a PRBS 215 - 1 at 10 Gbps signals respectively, are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Novel modal delay measurement for higher-order mode fiber using stretched pulse - based interferometry
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a novel modal delay measurement technique for higher-order mode fiber based on real-time optical frequency-domain reflectometry (OFDR) using an extremely simple, entirely passive and ultrafast wavelength sweeping mechanism, namely dispersion-induced optical pulse stretching.

articleTitle: Fiber Switching with a Diffractive Mirror Structure: Insertion Loss and Crosstalk Analysis
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We analyze the 1×K fiber switching performance when using a diffractive mirror in place of a tilting micromirror. Our findings demonstrate increasing insertion losses for larger fiber counts and elevated crosstalk levels due to quantization effects.

articleTitle: Transport of 8×2.5-Gb/s Wireless Signals over Optical Millimeter Wave through 12 Straight-Line WSSs and 160-km Fiber for Advanced DWDM Metro Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally show the first demonstration of a novel optical-wireless network by using WSS-based ROADMs in advanced DWDM metro networks. 8×2.5-Gb/s wireless signals are successfully transmitted over 160-km fiber with <;1.5-dB penalty in 12-cascaded WSSs networks.

articleTitle: Transmission and Transparent Wavelength Conversion for a Novel Return-to-Zero FSK Signal at 43 Gb/s
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate transmission over 100km SMF and transparent wavelength conversion based on a semiconductor optical amplifier for a 43 Gb/s return-to-zero frequency shift keying signal resulting in 4 dB over-all penalty.

articleTitle: 40-Gb/s in Plastic Optical Fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Plastic optical fiber together with appropriate low complexity transmitters and receivers are shown to allow high-performance optical links capable of supporting 40 Gb/s data rates over distances greater than 100 m.

articleTitle: Challenges and Solutions for 10 Gbps PON
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Technical feasibility and cost effectiveness of 10Gbps PON depend on requirements imposed by carriers. Coexistence with legacy PONs, support for 29 dB loss budget, symmetric transmission, and compatibility with analog video pose challenging but solvable problems.

articleTitle: Optical Technologies for Early GI Cancer Detection: Many Ways to Skin a Cat
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The article consists of a Powerpoint presentation on optical technologies for early GI cancer detection. The areas discussed include: optical diagnostics; white-light endoscopy; optical coherence tomography; microendoscopy; endocytology; fluorescence endoscopy; Raman spectroscopy; confocal microscopy; diffuse reflectance spectroscopy and elastic scattering spectroscopy etc. etc.

articleTitle: Dispersion Compensation of up to 25,200ps/nm Using IIR Filtering
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Digital infinite impulse response filtering is used to compensate for 25,200ps/nm of chromatic dispersion at 10G Baud accumulated in a recirculating loop.

articleTitle: Widely tunable digital concatenated grating DBR laser
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel, monolithic, widely tunable digital concatenated grating DBR laser for optical communications and sensors is proposed. Continuous tuning over 60 nm with high SMSRs and low threshold gains has been demonstrated here with simulated results.

articleTitle: Concepts and constraints of plasmonic waveguides operating from the visible to the THz regime
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A number of examples of metallic plasmon waveguides for high-confinement guiding of electromagnetic energy working in different parts of the spectrum are reviewed. While at visible frequencies, out-of-plane confinement below the diffraction limit is possible in simple planar geometries due to the efficient coupling of the electromagnetic field to the conduction electron plasma of the metal interfaces constituting the waveguide, at lower frequencies in the far-infrared a metamaterials approach is needed in order to engineer a plasmonic response through surface patterning. Additionally, an approach for efficient coupling of plasmon waveguides operating in the telecommunications window to optical fiber tapers is presented.

articleTitle: Waveband Assignment in Bi-directional Ring Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: In this paper, we give an integer linear programming formulation and present a heuristic algorithm to minimize the worst-case tuning ROADM range in a bi-directional ring network to support all-to-all traffic.

articleTitle: Advanced Multi-level Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Multi-level transmission having advantage of wider dispersion tolerance and narrower bandwidth, is one of the strong candidate for ultra high-speed serial interface. We review recent progress in multi-level systems, especially, incoherent multi-level receiver.

articleTitle: Single-Mode Tellurite Glass Holey Fiber with Extremely Large Mode Area for Infrared Applications
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report the fabrication of a very large mode area tellurite holey fiber from an extruded preform. Robust single-mode guidance with 3000 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> effective mode area was achieved and 2.9 dB/m loss was measured at 1.55 μm.

articleTitle: Novel Spectral Phase En/Decoder Based on Sampled Fiber Bragg Grating
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a novel spectral phase en/decoder based on sampled fiber Bragg grating. As a proof-of-principle, 15-chip spectral phase en/decoders are realized, and their en/decoding performance is verified by both numerical simulation and experimental demonstration.

articleTitle: Monitoring and Diagnostics of Power Anomalies in Transparent Optical Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Challenges in monitoring optically-transparent networks are highlighted for dynamically-controlled Raman amplification systems. We use models of amplifier physics together with statistical estimation to automatically discriminate between measurement errors, anomalous losses, and pump failures.

articleTitle: Ethernet Aggregation Approaches for Cell Tower Backhaul
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Review for Carrier Ethernet aggregation and transport for service providers seeking to evolve their existing investment while addressing Carrier Ethernet services. Technologies evaluated include VCAT, LCAS, RPR GFP-F, Ring and Point/Spoke topologies.

articleTitle: Long-Distance Quantum Communication with Multiple Quantum Memories
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The rate of entanglement generation between two distant nodes of a quantum repeater system is analytically evaluated. We consider multiple memories at each node and analyze the effect of residual entanglement on system throughput.

articleTitle: Chirp Frequency Synchronized Detection for Suppression of Light Interference in Optical Access Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel technique is proposed for suppressing light interference caused by the connection of noncompliant equipment. In this technique, the detected optical frequency is synchronized with the chirped frequency of a directly modulated laser diode.

articleTitle: Cost Efficient Survivable IP Over WDM With Dual Homing
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Dual homing lightpath service is considered to support survivable IP over WDM networks, where a prescribed fraction of network bandwidth must survive fiber-link faults. Network costs can decrease by as much as 32%.

articleTitle: Waveform Distortion Monitor for 160 Gbit/s Signal by Prescaled-clock Measurement using EA Modulator
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Novel waveform monitoring technique for 160 Gbit/s OTDM signal using an asynchronous EAM prescaler is proposed. This waveform monitor can detect waveform distortion caused by residual dispersion, PMD and OSNR degradation separately. And the feasibility of the monitor was examined by experiments and numerical estimations.

articleTitle: Photonic Crystal Fibers for Nonlinear Signal Processing
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Photonic crystal fiber offers possibilities for applications ranging from laser transmission to nonlinear optics for active devices due to its special properties. We describe some examples of using highly-nonlinear PCF for efficient optical signal processing.

articleTitle: A Radio-on-Hybrid WDM Transport System Based on Mutually Injection-Locked F-P LDs
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A radio-on-hybrid wavelength-division-multiplexing (WDM) transport system employing mutually injection-locked Fabry-Perot laser diodes (F-P LDs) is proposed and demonstrated. System performances evaluated by carrier to noise ratio (CNR), composite second order (CSO), composite triple beat (CTB), bit error rate (BER) for simultaneous transmission of CATV/LAN/ITS are improved. Our proposed systems are relatively simple and potentially low cost due to the use of mutually injection-locked F-P LDs as broadband light source (BLS).

articleTitle: Pseudowire System with VCCV Insertion (VI) in Optical Access Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new scheme, VCCV insertion (VI), to tackle the pseudowire system data transmission in optical access networks. We build a state space model for VI performance analysis. We prove that the VI scheme is both controllable and stable.

articleTitle: Structural optimization of ultimate low loss air-guiding photonic bandgap fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The surface-mode free condition for several structural-parameters is investigated in air-guiding photonic bandgap fiber (PBGF). We propose a novel type of PBGF without surface-modes which exhibits lower scattering losses as compared with 19-cell-core structures.

articleTitle: Coupling Control in Polymer Microring Based High-Q Filters and Electro-Optic Modulators Using Photobleaching
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Precise and fast post-fabrication trimming of coupling has been demonstrated using high-intensity laser photobleaching of the coupling region in high-Q passive polymer microrings vertically coupled to chromophore-doped waveguides, and in laterally coupled electro-optic ring modulators.

articleTitle: Acousto-optic mode coupling in photonic crystal fiber with structural imperfections
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We describe and theoretically analyze the origin of multiple resonance peaks experimentally observed in an all-fiber acousto-optic tunable filter built with a photonic crystal fiber having slightly deformed air-hole structure and non-circular outer cladding.

articleTitle: A Novel 10 Gb/s TDM-PON Using Embedded Clocks in Centralized Optical Signals and Conventional CW Receivers for Instantaneous Burst-Mode Data and Clock Recovery
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel 10 Gb/s TDM-PON architecture with embedded clocks in centralized optical signals is proposed. Using this scheme, 10 Gb/s burst-mode data and clock recovery through low-cost, conventional CW receivers have been designed and demonstrated.

articleTitle: Turbulent Square-Root Broadening of Fiber Lasers Output Spectrum
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The conventional RFL output spectrum and power are analytically described by the optical wave turbulence approach. The turbulent broadening can be also important in other types of fiber lasers, propagation phenomena and CW supercontinuum generation.

articleTitle: Transparent Path Length Optimized Optical Monitor Placement in Transparent Mesh Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Linear programming techniques are applied to the optimization of optical monitor placement by minimizing the worst case transparent path length in optical networks, which we study over different network topologies and traffic patterns.

articleTitle: Study of Nonlinearity and Dynamic Range of Coherent Optical OFDM Receivers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We study through theoretical analysis and simulate the nonlinearity and dynamic range for both balanced and single-ended receiver. The 0.5-dB Q-penalty dynamic range for single-ended receiver is 12 dB at laser RIN of -160 dBc/Hz

articleTitle: InP-Based High-Speed Photonic Devices
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The article consists of a Powerpoint presentation on InP-based high-speed photonic devices. The paper concludes that InP-based photonic devices demonstrated >80 Gbit/s operation; MZM and EA modulators for 80 Gbit/s and 100 Gbit/s; waveguide-integrated p-i-n photodiodes up to 160 Gbit/s; UTC-based photodiode >100 Gbit/s; high-power TWPD with >-2.5 dBm up to 150 GHz and high degree of integration is feasible.

articleTitle: Automatic PMD Compensation over Transoceanic Distance with Time Varying SOP, PSP, and PMD
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Automatic receiver PMD compensation was successfully demonstrated with 40Gb/s RZ- DPSK signals using a circulating loop transmission line. The long-term Q-factor histogram was significantly improved. PMD compensation was not as effective for the APol RZ-DPSK format.

articleTitle: InP-Based Photonic Devices; Focusing on devices for fiber-optic communications that monolithically integrate two or more functions
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The article consists of a PowerPoint presentation on InP-based photonic devices. The areas discussed include: InP basics; transmitters; inline devices; receivers; and fiber-optic communications. The paper concludes that InP is a very powerful platform, giving efficient optical gain, high-speed switching and modulation with low voltages, and efficient high-speed detection. We can surely expect more monolithically integrated InP devices in the marketplace in the future as research and increasing volumes drive down the cost of InP.

articleTitle: First Trial of Maintenance Friendly Network (MFN) by Switching Spare Field Fibers without Traffic Interruption
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Maintenance friendly network is demonstrated for first time with three SONET protection schemes fed into a ULH system. Traffic can be switched between six field fibers without triggering protection on 1+1, UPSR, or BLSR configurations.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Ultra-Compact Grating-Based 2×2 Beam Splitter for Miniature Photonic Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We provide detailed experimental study of reflectivity, insertion loss, and interference extinction ratio for our recently proposed and demonstrated grating-based beam splitter. Both low- loss and high-extinction-ratio devices are demonstrated for reflectivities close to 50%.

articleTitle: A Study of 160Gbps PON System Using OTDM and OCDM Technologies
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: First demonstration of asymmetric PON system (10 Gbps × 16 ch downstream) using OTDM and OCDM technologies is presented. We accomplished a transmission over 20 km SMF with optimized dispersion tolerance.

articleTitle: Development of "Cicada-Resistant" Optical Drop Cable with Protective Ribbon
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: "Cicada-resistant" optical drop cables with protective ribbons have been newly developed since optical fiber breakages of the conventional optical drop cable have often occurred in Japan due to laying eggs of cicadas.

articleTitle: Analysis of Brillouin-Based Distributed Fiber Sensors Using Optical Pulse Coding
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose the use of pulse Simplex-coding in distributed temperature sensors based on spontaneous Brillouin scattering. The analysis shows achieved performance improvement and the effect on stimulated Brillouin threshold, resulting in lower required input power.

articleTitle: 8×11.5-Gb/s OFDM Transmission over 1000km SSMF using Conventional DFB Lasers and Direct-Detection
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We show 8 × 11.5-Gb/s (10-Gb/s after coding) optical OFDM transmission over 1000 km SSMF with conventional DFB lasers and direct-detection. Compared with the coherent-detection using ECL lasers, DFB lasers and direct-detection can significantly reduce the system complexity and cost.

articleTitle: 40 Gb/s WDM NRZ-DPSK All-Optical Clock Recovery and Data Demodulation based on a Periodic Bragg Filter
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a novel optical circuit for the simultaneous demodulation and all-optical clock-recovery of 40 Gb/s WDM NRZ-DPSK signals. The circuit is based on an ad-hoc periodic FBG-filter. We report complete characterization in the whole C-band.

articleTitle: Towards a Deeper Understanding of Managing Dynamic Optical Networks Under Link Failures
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We quantify the impact of link failures after initial rerouting and show that some nodes continue to drop a significant portion of its traffic. We discuss the practical tradeoffs in rebalancing the network using redimensioning.

articleTitle: A Simple WDM-PON Architecture to Simultaneously Provide Triple-play Services by Using One Single Modulator
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Simple WDM-PON testbed with centralized-lightwave using single-arm IM to provide 10Gb/s data and 2.5Gb/s digital video downstream and 2.5Gb/s upstream data has been demonstrated. After 20km SSMF, power-penalty for all channels is less than 0.5dB.

articleTitle: Highly Nonlinear Bismuth-Oxide Fiber Based Dispersion Imbalanced Loop Mirror for Interferometric Noise Suppression
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a dispersion imbalanced loop mirror for interferometric noise suppression using a 32-cm highly nonlinear bismuth-oxide fiber. Improvement in the receiver sensitivity has been determined at different noise levels in a 10-Gb/s BER measurement.

articleTitle: High Resolution Optical Phase Response Measurement Using Single Sideband Modulation
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A high-resolution measurement to characterize the optical amplitude and phase is presented that uses single sideband modulation, a swept-wavelength tunable laser, and a Mach-Zehnder interferometer for frequency offset accuracy.

articleTitle: Fiber-Looped LiNbO3 Mach-Zehnder Modulator for 160 Gb/s Optical Time Division Demultiplexing and it's Comparison to an Electro-Absorption Modulator
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Optical time-division demultiplexing a 160 Gb/s signal to 40 Gb/s tributaries by novel method of LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> amplitude modulator connected in a fiber-loop demonstrates lower bit-error rate power penalty than using a high performance electro-absorption modulator.

articleTitle: Theoretical and Experiment Study of Resource Co-allocation Scheme in Optical Grid for Distributed Computing
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a minimum cost scheme to solve the co-allocation of application resource and network resource in optical grid. This scheme is deployed on a test-bed and its impact on performance is analyzed by experiment.

articleTitle: Evanescent Field Absorption Sensor in Aqueous Solutions using a Defected-core Photonic Crystal Fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A new absorption sensor is developed using a defected-core photonic crystal fiber with enhanced evanescent field. Excellent linearity is obtained between absorbance and concentration and length. The sensitivity is increased by more than sixty times compared with perpendicular direction measurement.

articleTitle: Generation of Radially Polarised Beams from Optical Fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We generate radially-polarised beams, for the first time with a novel, phase-engineered fiber that possesses these spatial patterns as stable eigenmodes. With conversion-efficiencies >99.7%, this is an attractive alternative to complex free-space techniques used currently.

articleTitle: Optimal Location Analysis of Two Interconnections for the Consolidation of Two Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: In the merging of two identical optimized optical networks with two minimal interconnection links, we analyze the optimal locations of the two interconnection links to achieve maximum saving in fiber links.

articleTitle: All-optical Amplitude Noise Suppression of 107 Gb/s DPSK Signals Using a Parametric Fiber Switch in a 320 km transmission experiment
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: An all-optical parametric fiber switch for all-optical amplitude noise suppression was applied mid-span in a 107 Gb/s differential phase shift keying (DPSK) transmission experiment. Using this switch an improved performance after 320 km transmission was achieved.

articleTitle: Experimental Assessment of a Direct Detection Optical OFDM System Targeting 10Gb/s and beyond
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We investigated a DD-O-OFDM system by variation of FFT-size, subcarrier usage and D/A-resolution. 63% usage of subcarriers was found as a limit for intermodulation penalties. By clipping 4 bit D/A-resolution at the transmitter is applicable.

articleTitle: Scalable Optical Multi-service Home Network
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a multi-service and scalable home network based on CWDM and broadcast and select technologies using single mode fiber. Network dimensioning is reported and the link budget is investigated in a multi-application configuration.

articleTitle: Optimized Chromatic Dispersion of DCMs in WDM Transmission Systems at 40Gbps
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We optimize the dispersion of DCMs by using an analytical expression of the achievable distance of WDM systems that is a function of losses & non-linearities and of the residual dispersion excursion over the C+-band.

articleTitle: A Novel Configuration for Both Mulitwavelength Mode-locking and Optical Clock Division
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Sextuple-wavelength mode-locking at 10 GHz and stable 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>, 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> and 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> clock divisions are realized exploiting the same configuration by incorporating dispersion compensation fiber with injected mode-locked fiber ring laser.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wide-Band Adiabatic Coupler As a Building Block for 2×32 PLC Splitter
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate adiabatic wavelength insensitive 2×2 PLC coupler with less than 0.6 dB variation over 1260- 1630 nm range and better than 0.25 dB PDL. We use it to build process tolerant 2×32 splitter having excellent optical performance.

articleTitle: Optical flip-flop based on coupled ultra-small Mach-Zehnder all-optical switches
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The configuration of coupled ultra-small Mach-Zehnder all-optical switches is quite attractive for high-speed optical flip-flops. Its bistability is experimentally demonstrated with an emulated setup. High-speed capability corresponding to 10 and 40 Gb/s is confirmed with simulation based on rate equation analysis.

articleTitle: Narrow Band Optical Parametric Amplification for Slow Light in Randomly Birefringent Fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The effects of random birefringence in narrowband parametric amplification for slow light has been numerically investigated showing that the reduction of the mean gain directly causes the reduction of the mean delay for small birefringence.

articleTitle: First Demonstration on the Non-transparency of PPLN and Its Potential Application of CSRZ-to-RZ Format Conversion
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report the experimental observation on the transparency and non-transparency aspects of PPLN by using NRZ-DPSK, RZ-DPSK, CSRZ-DPSK, and CSRZ signals. Potential non-transparent applications of 40 Gb/s tunable and multicasting CSRZ-to-RZ format conversions are experimentally demonstrated.

articleTitle: Direct-Detection Optical DPSK
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We investigate an MLSD-based optical receiver which enables effective detection of DPSK with only one photo-diode and without delay interferometer. The system exploits the uncompensated chromatic dispersion to deliver robust and reliable data detection.

articleTitle: Backoff-Channel Contention Resolution in Optical Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose backoff-channel contention resolution (BCCR) as a means of improving throughput in optical switched networks. Using BCCR, blocking can be reduced by orders of magnitude with little or no modification to existing hardware.

articleTitle: Preemption Window for Burst Differentiation in OBS
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper presents a novel control architecture for optical burst switching networks to efficiently apply burst preemption without the resources overbooking, which is specific to conventional OBS. Simulation results prove the effectiveness of this proposal.

articleTitle: Accumulated-Downtime-Aware Restoration Approach for Dynamic SLA-Differentiated Services in Survivable Mesh Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a novel restoration scheme by jointly considering accumulated downtime and SLA requirements of faulty connections. Results from simulation experiments demonstrate that the scheme achieves high restoration success rate and improves resource utilization.

articleTitle: High order ultrawideband pulse generation from NRZ-DPSK signals
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present ultrawideband doublet and triplet generation from NRZ-DPSK signals based on optical fiber and filter. Doublet and triplet are obtained by locating the optical carrier at the peak and slope of the filter, respectively.

articleTitle: Optical Testing for Passive Optical Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper reviews the demand for and the current status of PON optical diagnostics. Special focus is given to methods of optical testing that use capabilities that are incorporated into the transmission equipment itself.

articleTitle: Field demonstration of 10 Gbit/s transmission over a 37 ps PMD cable using electronic mitigation
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate the transmission at 10.7 Gbit/s over a high PMD link of 37 ps. The MLSE robustness allows transmission with sufficient operational margin and copes with the link polarization fluctuations.

articleTitle: High-Power Pulse Propagation in Optical Fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The operation of fiber lasers and amplifiers in new higher-power regimes for machining applications is limited by several nonlinear effects that must be understood and mitigated against for further development of these sources.

articleTitle: Novel Field Installable Sagged Fiber Connector Realizing Physical Contact Connection without Polishing Fiber Endface
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a new type of field installable optical fiber connector that enables us to realize physical contact connection by using a sharpened fiber endface and the compression force of sagged fiber.

articleTitle: Photonic Integrated Circuits with SOAs in WDM Optical Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Photonic integrated circuits (PICs) have had a significant impact on WDM transmission systems and are scalable, reliable, economic, and have performance comparable to discrete optoelectronic components. Integration of SOAs to the PIC platform extend the performance and benefits of PICs.

articleTitle: A Full-duplex Access Network based on CWDM-routed PONs
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The application of polarisation-division-multiplexing in presented, demonstrating full-duplex transmission in an access network architecture employing RSOA-based ONUs. Modelling of a single coarse-AWG OLT to transmit orthogonally-multiplexed burst-data and continuous-waves demonstrated crosstalk-free transmission up to 20 km.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of a Novel Cross-Layer Traffic Optimization Technique for Improving Throughput in Metro Ethernet/WDM Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: In metro Ethernet/WDM networks, it remains a challenge on how to improve performance through cross-layer traffic optimization. We experimentally study how to intelligently use L2 forwarding or L1 switching by monitoring the output queue size.

articleTitle: A Resource Pre-configuration Scheme in Intelligent Optical Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A resource pre-configuration scheme which forms a pre-configured topology has been proposed in intelligent optical networks. Simulations results show the connection establishing time of control plane could be significantly reduced by using resource pre-configuration strategy.

articleTitle: Long Distance Quantum Key Distribution in Optical Fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Results are presented from an experiment using quantum key distribution with decoy states and low- noise superconducting nanowire single photon detectors to distribute secure key across 145 km of optical fiber.

articleTitle: A Novel Multi-Stage Automatic PMD Compensator for Polarization-Multiplexed Signals
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel polarization controller and polarization mode dispersion compensator for polarization-multiplexed 42.656 Gb/s channels is presented. Tolerance for chromatic dispersion up to ±30 ps/nm and differential group delay up to 14 ps are measured.

articleTitle: 10 GHz-200 fs Pulse Generation with High Extension Ratio Using Mach-Zehnder-Modulator-Based Optical Comb Generator
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We have demonstrated simple and practical femtosecond pulse generation using Mach-Zehnder-modulator-based optical comb generator and adiabatic soliton compression techniques. 10-GHz, 200-fs pulses with excellent extinction ratio (>20-dB) were obtained.

articleTitle: Performance Impact of Multiple Access Interference in a 4-ary Pulse Position Modulated Optical Code Division Multiple Access (PPM/O-CDMA) System
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: An O-CDMA system utilizing 4-ary pulse position modulation and a novel virtual quadrant receiver is described. Bit-error-rates show the impact of multiple access interference, as influenced by its proximity to the correctly decoded signal.

articleTitle: Tunable Dispersion Compensation Using Parametric Processes
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This talk will discuss in detail the principle and potential applications of the intrinsically ultra-fast, wide-band and -range tunable dispersion compensation realized through parametric wavelength conversion in conjunction with dispersive fibers.

articleTitle: Quartzite: A Campus-Scale Hybrid Networking Infrastructure
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Quartzite is a hybrid wavelength - packet switched network on the campus of the University of California, San Diego. One of the key goals is to enable reconfigurations of the network at the physical (fiber, wavelength) and logical level (VLAN and routed) to support bandwidth intensive applications, non-standard protocols and other experiments that are usually incompatible with "production" networks. The structure of Quartzite is to connect laboratories on campus to a hybrid network core consisting of a standard, production switch router, and all-optical switch, and DWDM wavelength-selective switch (WSS). All components of Quartzite (except a custom-built WSS) are available as commodity parts. Most links feeding into the core are 10 Gigabit/s Ethernet (long reach grey, and C-band DWDM) with a smaller number of 1 gigabit/s links. More than 0.5 Terabit/s is currently provisioned to connect layer2 switches and directly-connected computing or storage endpoints. The entire infrastructure (including connected endpoints) can be reconfigured to suit the needs of specific experiments. The all-optical switching and wavelength switching are signal agnostic allowing non-ethernet transports to utilize the network/fiber infra-structure.

articleTitle: Channel Power Coupling in Constant Gain Controlled Amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Channel power coupling due to gain ripple and tilt in constant gain controlled erbium doped fiber amplifiers is measured in a transmission line and shown to grow in cascade.

articleTitle: Optimal Control of Tunable PMD Compensator Using Random Step Size Hill-Climbing Method
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a search control method of PMD compensator to decrease the possibility being trapped at local maxima. Transmission simulations at 160 Gb/s show that the method controls PMD compensator more optimally than conventional method.

articleTitle: Multi-user UWB-over-Fiber System based on High-chip-count Phase Coding
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: High-chip-count, phase-coded direct-sequence ultra wideband (UWB) signals for multiple access communications are generated in the optical domain, based on which a multi-user UWB-over-fiber system is proposed. A dual-user system is experimentally demonstrated.

articleTitle: Tolerance Analysis of 107 Gbit/s ETDM ASK-NRZ VSB
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report on the tolerances of a 107 Gbit/s ETDM ASK-NRZ VSB DWDM transmission system with respect to laser detuning, receiver filter detuning, DGD, residual chromatic dispersion and nonlinear transmission impairments.

articleTitle: Ultrahigh-Speed Multifunctional All-Optical Logic Gates Based on FWM in SOAs with PolSK Modulated Signals
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose ultrahigh-speed multifunctional all-optical logic gates AND, NOR, XNOR, S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>S¯<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, S¯<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, XOR, half adder, half subtracter, decoder and comparator based on four-wave mixing in semiconductor optical amplifiers with polarization-shift-keying modulated signals.

articleTitle: High Performance Photonics on Silicon
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Using silicon for optical interconnects would enable a platform for such a monolithic integration of optics and microelectronics. Photonics on silicon has been suggested since the 1980's. The challenge of using silicon as a photonic platform is the lack of strong active devices in silicon rich modulators, switches and detectors. Photodetectors on silicon with high performance are the one key node that remains to be demonstrated to enable photonic interconnections on a microelectronic chip. Optical switches for dense wavelength division multiplexing (DWDM) are key components for all optical networks on chip. Silicon photonics has attained much attention in recent years owing to the maturity of silicon in the electronic industry and its possibility to combine both photonic and electronic devices all on one chip.

articleTitle: Low bandwidth and cost-effective Brillouin frequency sensing using reference Brillouin-scattered beam
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a novel simple and cost-effective technique that can greatly reduce the electrical bandwidth for Brillouin frequency shift sensors from 11 to 0.2 GHz with only a reference fiber. Temperature change was also accurately observed. ©2008 Optical Society of America

articleTitle: Suppression of Rayleigh Scattering Noise in a TDM Multiplexed Interferometric Sensor System
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Suppression of Rayleigh induced noise in an interferometric sensor system employing pulsed heterodyne interrogation is demonstrated through a combination of coherence modulation and frequency shifting of noise within the sampling bandwidth. ≫40 dB suppression is achieved.

articleTitle: Self-Enclosed All-Fiber In-Line Etalon
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: An in-line fiber etalon, formed by a self-enclosed Fabry-Perot (F-P) cavity inside an optical fiber fabricated by using 157 nm laser micromachining, is first demonstrated. This etalon has almost perfect characteristics, such as excellent interferometric fringe visibility of up to ~30 dB, low thermal cross-sensitivity, great potential to realize mass-production with good reproducibility, low-cost, and super capability to operate in harsh environments, etc. It could be used as a precise wavelength reference or a practical strain sensor without any thermal compensation.

articleTitle: Development of Broadband Convergence Network and Services in Korea
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper presents the current developments of Broadband convergence Networks, Next Generation Networks, as well as emerging broadband convergence services in Korea.

articleTitle: High-Speed Modulation of Optical Injection-Locked Semiconductor Lasers
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We review the recent high-speed advances in optical injection-locked lasers, focusing on high resonance frequencies (> 70 GHz) and maximum bandwidth (> 40 GHz). Experimental and theoretical direct modulation and master amplitude and phase modulation are presented.

articleTitle: Physical Layer Impairment (PLI) Aware Transponder Selection Policies for GMPLS/WDM Optical Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We extend RSVP-TE protocol to handle the transponder parameters, availability at signaling time and propose two PLI-aware transponder selection policies: worst-first and best-first. The simulation results suggest that worst-first performs better w.r.t. blocking probability.

articleTitle: All-Optical Regeneration of DQPSK/QPSK Signals Based on Phase-Sensitive Amplification
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We investigate an all-optical (D)QPSK regenerator based on phase-sensitive amplifiers. Simulations show an MZ interferometer with one PSA in each arm can provide significant phase and amplitude noise suppression under optimal pump conditions.

articleTitle: Ultrafast measurement of phase distribution of DPSK signals using 1-symbol delayed dual-channel linear optical sampling
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We observe the phase distribution of DPSK signals using a newly developed 1-symbol delayed dual-channel linear optical sampling. This method has the potential to measure ultrafast signals with a symbol rate of greater than 100-Gbit/s.

articleTitle: Optical vs. electronic chromatic dispersion compensation in WDM coherent PM-QPSK systems at 111 Gbit/s
publicationTitle: OFC/NFOEC 2008 - 2008 Conference on Optical Fiber Communication/National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
